definitions.gloss: secret informing; tip-off; informing on someone
definitions.explanation: Secretly reporting someone's wrongdoing to the authorities or to someone in power. Carries a negative connotation of betrayal or disloyalty.

examples.japanese: ⟦{仲間|なかま}→仲間：03498_nakama⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{密告|みっこく}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
{密告|みっこく}⟦によって→によって：06801_niyotte⟧⟦{犯人|はんにん}→犯人：03572_hannin⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{逮捕|たいほ}→逮捕：03397_taiho⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The criminal was arrested thanks to a tip-off.

examples.japanese: ⟦{戦時中|せんじちゅう}→戦時中：28629_senjichuu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{隣人|りんじん}→隣人：10007_rinjin⟧⟦による→による：28349_niyoru⟧{密告|みっこく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{恐|おそ}れられていた→恐れる：02023_osoreru⟧。
examples.english: During wartime, people feared being informed on by their neighbors.

notes:
{密告|みっこく} means secretly reporting someone's wrongdoing to authorities or those in power. It carries a strong negative connotation of betrayal and treachery.

COMPOUNDS:
- {密告|みっこく}⟦{者|しゃ}→〜者：04662_sha⟧: informer, snitch
- {密告|みっこく}⟦{状|じょう}→状：09878_jou⟧: letter of denunciation
- ⟦{匿名|とくめい}→匿名：11797_tokumei⟧{密告|みっこく}: anonymous tip-off

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {密告|みっこく}: secret informing (negative — implies betrayal)
- ⟦{通報|つうほう}→通報：14318_tsuuhou⟧: reporting to authorities (neutral)
- ⟦{告発|こくはつ}→告発：07999_kokuhatsu⟧: formal accusation, whistleblowing (can be positive)
- ⟦{告|つ}げ{口|ぐち}→告げ口：08453_tsugeguchi⟧: tattling, telling on someone (childish)

ETYMOLOGY:
⟦{密|みつ}→密：03777_mitsu⟧ (secret) + {告|こく} (inform, tell). The ⟦{密|みつ}→密：03777_mitsu⟧ emphasizes the secretive, underhanded nature of the act.

USAGE:
Often appears in historical and wartime contexts. In modern usage, also refers to anonymous tips to police or tax authorities.
